## Purpose

Repair proven CI failures inherited from an epic target when the batch itself
seals the epic subtree. Work stays on the retained candidate, preserving previous
repairs and frozen sources. The train normally files this repair automatically.

## When a playbook uses it

A local operator or live owning supervisor can inspect a stuck red epic batch
and request its ordinary repair explicitly. Start with a preview; apply requires
the previewed candidate and target SHAs and a nonblank reason. Ordinary workers
and playbook service principals cannot invoke the control directly.

## How it works internally

`TrainControls.repair_target` checks that the open batch seals its own non-default
epic target, observes both refs, and compares trusted required checks for their
exact commits. Apply refreshes those checks and calls `OrdinaryRepairService.allocate`
with the same authorization, lease and attempt budget used by automatic repair.
It rechecks both refs and the frozen sources before a new allocation.

## Side effects and persistence

Preview does not allocate work. Apply files or reuses an ordinary root bugfix on
the candidate ref. A new allocation records its task, repair input, branch fence
and batch attempt count transactionally. It does not reopen the epic, add a child
or advance the target. Publication still requires trusted green CI on the exact
repaired candidate and preservation of every frozen member.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`refused` includes a changed head, unavailable or inconclusive CI evidence,
paused or unrelated batch, unconfirmed source or branch ownership, and an
exhausted repair budget. Inspect `aq integration status PROJECT`
and preview again after correcting the cause. This control does not reset budgets
or override operator holds. A caller without operator or owning supervisor
authority receives `unauthorized`.

## Example step

From an authorized supervisor CLI session:

```sh
aq integration repair-target BATCH_ID
aq integration repair-target BATCH_ID --apply \
  --candidate-sha CANDIDATE_SHA_FROM_PREVIEW \
  --target-sha TARGET_SHA_FROM_PREVIEW --reason "Repair inherited epic CI failures"
```
